input: Adsorption of a dye from water on a zeolite 13X sample was measured in batch tests at 298 K. In a batch test a known mass of adsorbent is held in contact with the dye solution and the concentration is followed as uptake proceeds, so each test gives both the rate at which the dye leaves the water and the loading the adsorbent reaches. The fitted Langmuir capacity was 212 mg of dye per gram of adsorbent at pH 5. The capacity is a parameter of the Langmuir fit, not a single measured loading: it is the loading the fitted relation approaches as the concentration rises, and it summarises the whole set of equilibrium points at pH 5 in one number. Removal in a single test depends on how much adsorbent is present. At an adsorbent dose of 0.8 g L-1, removal after 120 min was 87% of the initial dye concentration of 50 mg L-1. The two figures answer different questions. The capacity states what the zeolite 13X can hold at equilibrium under the fitted relation, while the removal states what one dose achieved in 120 min from one starting concentration. The Langmuir fit is reported for pH 5 only; capacity at other pH values was not measured. The 212 mg g-1 figure is therefore a pH 5 result, and adsorption performance away from pH 5 is not established by these tests.
